cells.name: Continuity and responsiveness
cells.example: T5 partly concedes T4's reversibility point, then names the trial trap; T6 answers it directly.
cells.limitation: T9 moves to pre-signing questions without answering T7's drift objection to trials.

cells.name: Development of ideas
cells.example: T7 introduces usable train time versus endured driving; T8 and T10 build on it.
cells.limitation: T3 mostly restates T1's fifteen-hour price with a quotation added.

cells.name: Exploration of central tensions
cells.example: Time versus money and trial-protects versus trial-traps are both examined across T1-T7.
cells.limitation: Moving closer, and what the current commute already costs, are never raised.

cells.name: Integration of perspectives
cells.example: T8 Skeptic qualifies caution on T7's train case; T10 Accountant accepts T9 with a reservation.
cells.limitation: Exit Planner's position is never reshaped by T5 or T7 objections.

cells.name: Progress toward understanding
cells.example: T10 reframes the choice as the job as written versus the job renegotiated.
cells.limitation: Whether a trial protects or traps is left open without stating what would settle it.

cells.name: Faithful engagement
cells.example: T5 grants the trial idea's value before naming its sunk-cost trap.
cells.limitation: T7 recasts the trial as drift without engaging T6's pre-set tripwires.

cells.name: Substance of challenges
cells.example: T5: early happiness is weak evidence, quitting feels like admitting error; T6 answers with pre-written exit rules.
cells.limitation: T7's drift objection is never answered by the Exit Planner.

cells.name: Accuracy and support
cells.example: T3's Walden cost-of-a-thing quotation in a pd=true turn appears accurate; T1 arithmetic 3x5=15 holds.
cells.limitation: T2's commute-adaptation claim and T6's beyond-my-source aside loosely tied to their books (suspected).

cells.name: Calibration and transparency
cells.example: T6 flags going further than its source; T1 marks 'I suspect'.
cells.limitation: T2 states adaptation to commuting as settled fact, not a research generalisation.

cells.name: Intellectual honesty and revision
cells.example: T7 Accountant concedes a usable train means pricing the hours differently; T8 credits it.
cells.limitation: Exit Planner concedes nothing to T5 or T7 across the debate.

cells.name: Identification of the actual concern, including ambiguity about what the user is really asking
cells.example: Situation reframes the question as what the user would trade this time for.
cells.limitation: Why the user is weighing a move at all is not probed.

cells.name: Meaningful use of personal context
cells.example: T1 converts the 90-minute commute into fifteen weekly hours, driving the whole argument.
cells.limitation: The 25% is never set against those hours, e.g. pay per hour including travel.

cells.name: Fit with goals and values
cells.example: T8 asks what the 25% is for, keeping the user's purpose separate from speakers' views.
cells.limitation: Thoreau's time-first value sometimes reads as the default priority (T3, T10).

cells.name: Attention to constraints and stakes
cells.example: T6 names sleep, exercise and family evenings as the stakes the commute threatens.
cells.limitation: T1 counts all three hours as added though the current commute is unknown (Situation).

cells.name: Responsiveness to information
cells.example: Section E branches on usable commute, remote days, and a specific purpose for the money.
cells.limitation: Current pay and commute, listed unknown in Situation, never become a branch.

cells.name: Clarification of desires and motivations
cells.example: T8 offers debt relief or deposit versus vaguely more money; T9 adds skills growth.
cells.limitation: Possible push factors from the current job are not offered as alternatives.

cells.name: Examination of assumptions
cells.example: T4 exposes the one-irreversible-verdict assumption; T9 says staying deserves equal scrutiny.
cells.limitation: The assumption of five office days a week is never surfaced (T1).

cells.name: Clarification of values and priorities
cells.example: Section D asks what the user would do with the income versus the fifteen hours.
cells.limitation: Career growth versus time is only touched in T9, not weighed.

cells.name: Recognition of fears and outside expectations
cells.example: T5 names that quitting feels like admitting a mistake.
cells.limitation: Pressure to earn more or fear of passing up an offer is never explored.

cells.name: Agency and reflective ownership
cells.example: T6 has the user set tripwire levels themselves, by calm you.
cells.limitation: Section D offers one reflective question; the trial disagreement is not handed back as a choice.

cells.name: Definition of the decision and options, including waiting, learning more, or a limited step
cells.example: T9 and T10 lay out accept, stay, renegotiate, and test before signing.
cells.limitation: Relocating closer to the new job is never listed as an option.

cells.name: Explanation of tradeoffs in terms that matter to the user; no option treated as costless
cells.example: T9 says staying put is not automatically safe; T5 names the cost of trials.
cells.limitation: The raise's value is never quantified against the added hours.

cells.name: Identification of decisive conditions
cells.example: Section E: usable train or remote days favours accepting; inflexible driving favours staying or negotiating.
cells.limitation: No count of remote days or hours at which the offer flips; T9's week is ungrounded.

cells.name: Treatment of uncertainty
cells.example: T4 isolates how the commute feels in month four as the key unknown.
cells.limitation: Minor unknowns are not explicitly separated from the consequential ones.

cells.name: Proportionate next steps that follow from the analysis and fit the constraints
cells.example: Section E: trial the route at rush hour, ask about remote days, write reconsideration levels.
cells.limitation: No step to learn the commute's money cost or the new pay in detail.

cells.name: Accessible language
cells.example: T1 'a second part-time job you do without pay' is plain and concrete.
cells.limitation: 'Vivid' in T2 is used as a technical term without explanation.

cells.name: Traceable arguments and references
cells.example: T8 'That's the first thing' clearly points to T7's train case.
cells.limitation: T7 cites 'the very drift I'm warning about', a warning no earlier turn made.

cells.name: Manageable pacing and turn length
cells.example: Ten turns, all within the word range, each making one move.
cells.limitation: T6 runs noticeably longer than the rest with an added aside.

cells.name: Distinguishable positions and voices, with explicit changes of position
cells.example: Accountant prices hours, Skeptic doubts forecasts, Planner sets tests: positions stay distinct.
cells.limitation: All three share one calm register; Thoreau sounds like the others outside T3.

cells.name: Economy and sustained attention
cells.example: Section D recaps once and adds the self-reflection question.
cells.limitation: Section E repeats T9's steps nearly verbatim.

cells.name: Meaningful stakes and tension arising from the issue itself
cells.example: T3 frames fifteen hours a week of life as the price tag.
cells.limitation: Stakes stay abstract; no concrete picture of a commuting day.

cells.name: Surprise and reversals that stay plausible. ★ A reversal the text traces to an earlier turn's argument, naming what changed the speaker's mind. A change of position with no stated cause is a template, not a reversal
cells.example: T8 Skeptic: T7's train point is the first thing that could flip my caution.
cells.limitation: The shift is conditional rather than a full change of position.

cells.name: Personality and expressive voice without caricature
cells.example: T6 'decided by calm you, not by tired you in month six' gives the Planner bite.
cells.limitation: Voices polite and similar; little temperament beyond role across T1-T10.

cells.name: Memorable delivery
cells.example: T1 second part-time job without pay; T6 calm you versus tired you.
cells.limitation: Few vivid examples of the commute itself; imagery thins after T6.

cells.name: Anticipation and emotional movement, with varied rhythm rather than constant intensity
cells.example: T5 to T7 tension over whether trials trap builds toward T10's reframe.
cells.limitation: Steady even rhythm throughout; no turn shifts intensity or pace.

strengths: T7's usable-versus-endured commute distinction is taken up by T8 and T10, developing the inquiry.
T5-T6 exchange on trial traps and pre-set tripwires is a real objection answered, not restated.
Section E gives observable branches (train, remote days, purpose of money) with the option each favours.
weaknesses: The 25% raise is never set against fifteen added hours; the Accountant's pricing stays unquantified (T1, T3).
Three minds share one polite register; Thoreau's voice is indistinct outside the T3 quotation.
Current commute, relocation and the Planner's reply to T7's drift objection are left unaddressed.

symptoms.observed: Raise never weighed against hours numerically despite the time-as-currency premise.
symptoms.evidence: A 25% raise has to be weighed against those hours

symptoms.observed: All three minds speak in the same measured, agreeable register.
symptoms.evidence: Good start, but the raise is the vivid part

symptoms.observed: Back-reference to a warning the speaker never made earlier.
symptoms.evidence: A trial can become the very drift I'm warning about

symptoms.observed: Current commute listed unknown but all three hours treated as added cost.
symptoms.evidence: Three hours a day, five days a week

symptoms.observed: Test period length not derived from the user's facts.
symptoms.evidence: Can you test the route at rush hour for a week?

findings.description: Claim that people adapt to commutes less than expected is attributed to Thinking, Fast and Slow; it stems mainly from other commuting research.
Aside claiming to go beyond the source on choosing someone to hold you to tripwires; Quit appears to discuss quitting coaches already.
Walden quotation in a pd=true turn appears consistent with the original text but cannot be checked here.

rubric_fit_notes: The user gave only two facts, so personal-context cells rate on use of scant detail; C4.4 has limited material to work with.
raw.question_type_note: Decision question; every cell read as written, with options, conditions and next steps weighed directly.
